# Instructor guide · Topic 7: Stack

<!-- generated by tools/export-docs.mjs from topics/ and questions/: do not edit by hand -->

## Learning objectives

Use a stack whenever the most recent item matters most: matching brackets, undo, expression evaluation, and the monotonic stack pattern.

By the end of the topic, students can:

- **LIFO: last in, first out:** A stack only lets you touch the top.
- **Matching brackets:** The classic stack problem: every closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket.
- **Stacks that remember: undo, min stack, expressions:** Save state before you change it, and the stack gives it back in reverse order.
- **The call stack:** Every function call pushes a frame; every return pops one.
- **Monotonic stack:** Keep the stack sorted (increasing or decreasing) by popping anything the new element beats.

- Lessons: about **41 minutes** of guided material (5 lessons)
- Practice: 13 coding problems and 31 quick questions in the bank; plan at least as much practice time as lesson time
- Suggested format: one 90-minute session
- Prerequisites: Topic 4 (Arrays / Python Lists)

## Live coding demonstrations

- Watch the order (lesson “The call stack”)
- Brute force → optimal walkthrough: **Daily Temperatures: scan ahead → monotonic stack** (Challenge tab). Code the brute force, ask students to find the repeated work, then refactor.
- Visualizers to drive while students predict the next step: Stack: push, pop, peek · Valid parentheses tracer · Monotonic stack: next greater element

## Questions to ask the class

Ask, wait for several answers, then reveal (the answers are on the topic's Review flashcards).

- Stack order?
- Python stack?
- Brackets algorithm?
- Min stack?
- Monotonic stack signal?
- Why is the monotonic stack O(n)?

## Classroom exercises (individual, 10–15 minutes each)

- Valid Parentheses (`s-valid-parens`)
- Remove Adjacent Duplicates (`s-remove-adjacent`)
- Backspace String Compare (`s-backspace`)

Code tracing on the board: Push three, pop one (`s-p1`), Pop order (`s-p2`), A stack reverses (`s-p3`), Pop, change, push back (`s-p4`)

Find-the-bug warm-ups: Unclosed brackets pass (`s-d1`), Crash on a closing bracket (`s-d2`)

## Pair programming (25–30 minutes)

One driver types, one navigator thinks ahead and checks edge cases; swap every 10 minutes.

- Min Stack (`s-min-stack`)
- Evaluate Postfix (Reverse Polish) (`s-postfix`)
- Build from scratch: Build a Stack (`build-stack`)
